name: Polyarticular Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ILAR Classification Criteria for Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

criteria.description: Arthritis affecting five or more joints during the first six months of disease
Onset of arthritis before 16 years of age
Exclusion of other causes of arthritis such as infectious, autoimmune, or malignancy
Presence or absence of rheumatoid factor (RF) positivity defines subtypes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Arthritis in five or more joints for at least six weeks with onset before age 16, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Rheumatoid factor positivity distinguishes RF-positive and RF-negative polyarticular JIA subtypes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical polyarthritis involving small and large joints
searchTerms: arthritis in small and large joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Morning joint stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
searchTerms: stiff joints in morning over 30 minutes
swollen joints with thickened joint lining
joint swelling due to synovial growth
reduced range of motion in joints
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

rare.symptomName: Neuropathic pain due to peripheral neuropathy
searchTerms: burning or shooting pain in limbs

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Positive rheumatoid factor (RF) in RF-positive subtype
Antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity in some cases
imaging: Joint space narrowing and erosions on X-ray
Synovial hypertrophy and effusion on ultrasound
MRI showing synovitis and bone marrow edema
other: Synovial fluid analysis showing inflammatory profile

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of quotidian fever and rash
Acute onset with single joint involvement

references: Petty RE, et al. International League of Associations for Rheumatology classification of juvenile idiopathic arthritis: second revision. J Rheumatol. 2004.
Giancane G, et al. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis: diagnosis and treatment. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2016.
Orphanet: Polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis. ORPHA:404580.
